correctness.rationale: For the normalized complex-gradient Poisson energy, the mode z^n has exact symbol n²∫_0^1 t^(n-1)(1-t)(1-c log(1-t))dt = n/(n+1)[1+c(H_{n+1}-1)]. The signed Poisson mixing factor v(t)=t/(1-t)-log(1-t)-1 has one sign crossing. Its Poisson integral J_v(pi)=1-3log2+2Li_2(1/2)=0.08503951125...>0; ratios P_t(theta1)/P_t(theta2) strictly increase in t when theta1<theta2, proving J_v(theta)>0 and strictly decreasing for every angle. Independent positive quadratures at pi,2,1,0.4 confirm this but do not substitute for the single-crossing proof. Fourier Poisson moments give exactly the asserted positive jump form. Near theta=0, P_(1-s)(theta)/s approximates 2/(s²+theta²), yielding c*pi/|theta| with logarithmic remainder, hence c=0 finite mass one versus all c>0 infinite activity. The origin expansion gives Δw_c(0)=4(c-1), so c>1 truly lies outside superharmonic weights.
